changes.title: Amazon Aurora and RDS now support Graviton5-based R9g database instances
changes.detail: AWS Graviton5-based R9g database instances are now generally available for Amazon Aurora with PostgreSQL compatibility and MySQL compatibility, and for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB. Graviton5-based R9g instances provide up to a 30% performance improvement and up to a 22% price-performance improvement for on-demand pricing over Graviton4-based instances of equivalent sizes on Amazon Aurora, depending on database engine, version, and workload. changes.title: Amazon SNS now supports push notifications in four additional AWS Regions
changes.detail: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) now supports sending push notifications in the Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Europe (Zurich), and AWS GovCloud (US-East) Regions. Amazon SNS is a fully managed pub/sub service that provides message delivery to multiple endpoints, including AWS Lambda, Amazon SQS, Amazon Data Firehose, HTTP, SMS (via AWS End User Messaging), push notifications, and email. changes.title: Google Kubernetes Engine: Change (November 12, 2026)
changes.detail: In GKE version 1.35.1-gke.1516000 or later, GKE Dataplane V2 clusters use a unified cilium-cni configuration instead of a chained CNI setup. With this change, Cilium configures the Pod default gateway by using its node-local virtual router interface ( cilium_host ), which has the statically assigned link-local IP address 169.254.4.6 . As a result, node-local kubelet health checks ( kube-probe for liveness, readiness, and startup probes) and NodeLocal DNSCache traffic now originate from 169.254.4.6 instead of the .1 address of the node's Pod CIDR range (for example, 10.x.x.1 ).
